title: Umrah and Hajj
hookLine: the lesser pilgrimage any time, the greater in Dhul Hijjah

cards: Two travel bookings to Mecca. One is for a week in early spring, the dates picked to fit a school break.

The other is for a fixed handful of days in a fixed month, booked through an agency with a waiting list, and it can't be moved by a single day. Both travelers will put on white. Both will walk around the Kaaba.
One is going on umrah, the other on Hajj. From the outside they can look almost the same. They aren't.

teach.b: First, the verse that names both. Surah two of the Qur'an, in Pickthall's words: "Perform the pilgrimage and the visit (to Mecca) for Allah." The pilgrimage is Hajj.
The visit is umrah. Second, when.
Umrah can be made at any time of the year. Hajj has its own days in its own month, Dhul Hijjah, and outside those days there is no Hajj. That's why one booking moves and the other doesn't.
Third, what's inside. Umrah is short: entering the pilgrim's state, ihram; walking around the Kaaba, the tawaf; walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah; and cutting or shaving the hair.
Hajj holds those rites and adds more: the standing at Arafah we met this week, the night at Muzdalifah, the days at Mina. Fourth, lesser and greater.

teach.h: THE DAY OF THE GREATER PILGRIMAGE.
teach.b: Surah nine speaks of "the day of the Greater Pilgrimage," and some scholars read that phrase as setting Hajj beside a lesser pilgrimage, the umrah. Lesser doesn't mean worthless.
A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari says one umrah to the next wipes away what falls between them, and an accepted Hajj has no reward but Paradise.

The schools differ on how binding umrah is: the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools hold it a duty once in a life for those able; the Hanafi and Maliki schools, a strongly recommended practice. Each gives its reasons.
And this week, end to end: two special fasts, a hidden night, a short line asking pardon, a fast kept safely, two joys, a door marked if able, and today, two pilgrimages, one lesser and one greater.

how: Muslims make umrah at any time of year, sometimes more than once, and make Hajj in Dhul Hijjah on its set days; some combine the two in one journey during the Hajj season.

games.q: you want to go to Mecca this spring, outside Dhul Hijjah. which journey can you make?
o: Hajj, if you book early enough.
neither; Mecca is closed outside Hajj.
games.why: umrah. Hajj only happens on its set days in Dhul Hijjah; the visit can be made any time.

practice: Say it to yourself slowly: umrah, any time of year, ihram, the walk around the Kaaba, the walk between two hills, the cut of the hair. Hajj, only in Dhul Hijjah: all of that, and Arafah, Muzdalifah and Mina.
If you know someone who has made either journey, picture their face and think of asking them about it.
